I farm 6.5 mu myself, so I will not play with big changes. I have high school education and 50 years in the field, so I look at it from yield, cost, and timing together. In Quzhou, wheat-maize is a tight rotation. If I miss one operation, the next crop suffers. My land has well irrigation, so I will lean on stable water and keep fertilizer a little on the safe side. I would rather spend some extra yuan on fertilizer than lose grain on 6.5 mu, because on a small area yield loss hurts more than a bit of overuse.

For wheat, I will keep improved seed and steady water. Wheat here responds well when the stand is even and the topdressing is not late. I will aim for around 20 kg nitrogen per mu, with 9 kg phosphorus and 5 kg potassium. I will split the nitrogen, putting part down with base fertilizer and the rest at jointing, because that is where I usually see the return. With well water, I will plan 3 irrigations if the season is normal: one around overwintering or green-up depending on soil moisture, one at jointing, and one at grain filling if the field is dry. I will do 2 pesticide sprays for wheat as a working plan, mainly to keep aphids and disease from building. I will use rotary tillage ahead of wheat because it fits my scale and leaves a workable seedbed without costing me too much labor.

For maize, I will stay with hybrid seed. That is not the place to save money. After wheat harvest, time is tight, so I will direct seed or disturb the soil as little as possible; no-tillage saves time and keeps moisture. I will put maize a little higher on potassium than wheat because stalk strength and grain filling matter, and lodged maize is a headache. I will target about 19 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 6 kg potassium per mu. I will give 2 irrigations as my base plan, one around the big jointing-to-tasseling demand and one at grain filling if rain is short. I will plan 2 pesticide applications, not because I like spraying, but because once armyworm, aphids, or leaf disease get ahead, the crop falls fast. On my acreage, I want steady yield more than gambling on saving one pass.
